deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): two superposed systems, layers A and B, sit a small distance 2ε apart. If the first system's charge on B produces potential F(x,y), the matching charge on A produces -F(x+2ε,y). The total is F(x,y) - F(x+2ε,y) = -2ε ∂F/∂x - ε² ∂²F/∂x² - ..., and only the first term is kept. This is the potential of a double layer of moment 2ε·(density).

This page:
(1) Riemann identifies F'(x,y) = ∂F/∂x as the component, parallel to the x-axis, of the force that the first system exerts on a charge element at (x,y). The sign is ignored, since force = -grad potential.

(2) He announces a general lemma about this normal component. A plane carries an agent of uniform density ρ, bounded by an arbitrary figure. The point p lies at perpendicular distance x from the plane. The goal is the force on p.

(3) Polar subdivision of the plane:
- Rays from the foot P of the perpendicular cut the plane into elementary sectors. A marginal insertion defines θ as the angle a sector makes with an arbitrary initial line, so the opening is dθ.
- Each plane through the perpendicular is cut into sectors with vertex at p. φ is the angle a sector makes with the x-axis (the perpendicular), so the opening is dφ.
- The second subdivision of the plane (completed on the next page) uses circles about P of radius r = x tan φ.

Completion from the next page (not on this page, given for clarity):
- Area element: dA = r dθ dr = x tanφ dθ · x sec²φ dφ = x² tanφ sec²φ dφ dθ.
- Distance: |Pp| = x sec φ.
- Inverse-square force: ρ dA / (x² sec²φ) = ρ tanφ dφ dθ.
- Normal (x) component: multiply by cos φ, giving ρ sinφ dφ dθ = ρ dΩ.

Here dΩ is the projection of the area element onto the unit sphere about p. Hence the normal force component of a uniform plane lamina equals ρ times the solid angle the lamina subtends at p. Consequently the double-layer potential equals the moment times the solid angle. This is the geometric tool announced on the previous page in place of 'verwickelte Doppelintegrale'.
errors: Sign convention: ∂F/∂x is minus the x-component of force (for force = -grad V). Riemann explicitly disregards signs ('vom Zeichen absieht' on the next page), so this is harmless.
Notation 'durch x gelegte Ebene' uses x both for the distance and for the perpendicular line/axis. This is a mild ambiguity, not an error.
No mathematical errors on this page; it is set-up only. The computation completed on the next page is correct.

results.what: First-order expansion of the potential of two oppositely charged parallel layers 2ε apart. The potential is -2ε ∂F/∂x, the x-component of the field of one layer.
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (1839/40); Helmholtz (1853) for electrical double layers

results.what: Normal component of attraction of a uniform plane lamina at a point equals density times the solid angle subtended. Proved by subdivision into conical elements with area element x² tanφ sec²φ dφ dθ.
results.modern_name: Solid-angle formula for the normal field of a uniform plane sheet (field of a double layer = moment × solid angle)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Allgemeine Lehrsätze (1839/40); classical potential theory (Green, Chasles)

deep.surprise_reason: The solid-angle lemma for a uniform plane lamina and the double-layer potential were classical by 1853 (Gauss, Helmholtz). Riemann's geometric derivation is careful but standard; it is notable only as evidence of his early work on electrostatics of layered systems.

checkable.asserts: d(x tanφ) = x dφ / cos²φ, giving the radial width of the circle subdivision (equals 0).
Area element divided by squared distance (x secφ)² equals tanφ dφ dθ (equals 0).
The normal component of the elementary force is ρ sinφ dφ dθ, the solid-angle element (equals 0).
An infinite uniform plane subtends solid angle 2π, giving normal field 2πρ (equals 0).
F(x)-F(x+2ε) = -2ε F'(x) - 2ε² F''(x) + ... ; note the ε² coefficient is -2F'', whereas the previous page writes -F''ε².

transcription_corrections: Lines 4-6: read 'welche von dem ersten Systeme auf [-einen-] ein im Punkte x, y befindliches Elektricitätstheilchen ausgeübt wird'. 'ein' and 'im' are written above the struck word, and the marginal 'befindliches Elektricitätstheilchen' is inserted at the mark F. The reading 'den Punkte x, y in F' is wrong.

The marginal insertion at the second mark after 'haben' reads: 'den Winkel den ein solcher Elementar-Sektor mit einer beliebigen Anfangslinie macht nenne man θ und demgemäß die Öffnung [dθ]'. It does not read '{+F befindliches Elektricitätstheilchen+}', which belongs to the first insertion.
In the marginal note, 'Elementar-' is written above 'Sektors', and 'von x' after 'Sektors' is struck.
The paragraph 'Jede durch x gelegte Ebene … Öffnung dφ' is crossed by several vertical strokes in the manuscript, possibly marking deletion or revision. This is not indicated in the transcription.
'sei dθ' after 'Sektors': 'sei' appears partly struck/overwritten. The final sense is retained via the marginal insertion.
